headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure from residential users to large energy users, primarily data centers, and extends energy assistance programs.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, environmental advocates (e.g., Piedmont Environmental Council), consumer advocates, Virginia Democrats.
opponents: Data center industry (implied, as the bill shifts costs to them). Dominion Energy initially sought to recover costs from all ratepayers.
news_headline: Virginia Regulators Order Data Centers to Pay for Grid Upgrades
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission directed Dominion Energy to draft a policy charging data centers for grid improvements exclusively for their facilities. This move aims to shift hundreds of millions of dollars in transmission costs away from households and small businesses.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water supplied to data centers, increasing transparency on their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan (sponsor), Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, environmental groups (e.g., Sierra Club Virginia Chapter, Piedmont Environmental Council), policymakers, water resource planners.
opponents: Data centers (implied, as they previously withheld water usage as an industry secret).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report water volumes delivered to data centers. This legislation addresses concerns about the lack of centralized tracking of data center water use, especially as the industry expands.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles and potential impacts on local resources before local approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Thomas (sponsor), Delegate Guzman, Delegate Helmer, Delegate McAuliff, Delegate Reid, Delegate Carr, Delegate Keys-Gamarra, Delegate Rasoul, Delegate Reaser, Delegate Singh, Faith Alliance for Climate Solutions (FACS), local communities.
opponents: Data center industry (implied, as it adds regulatory hurdles).
news_headline: Data Center Transparency Bill Passed by Virginia General Assembly
news_summary: HB 153, sponsored by Delegate Josh Thomas, requires local governments to conduct site assessments for new high-energy facilities, including noise levels and water supply impact. This aims to provide critical information before approving construction near residential areas and schools.
